- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; increase downward adjustment or add lagged momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or add decay factor.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often continues upward trend; reduce forecast slope or apply smoothing filter.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong volatility, model underestimates volatility; add stochastic or range-based adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); adjust forecast to reflect sentiment + recent volatility in final 10–15 days.
